episode.title: Restore the desktop packaging toolchain in isolated installer stages and report missing prerequisites as failure
episode.before: At parent commit 77bb64813cb987ad80236219a20c6cb549b40049, the explicitly requested desktop stage entered the checkout and called the desktop builder without first restoring the managed Node directory to PATH. Because each stage ran in a separate process, npm could be absent even when Node had been provisioned earlier. The builder treated that condition as a successful skip by warning and returning 0, allowing the stage protocol to emit an ok result despite producing no desktop application.
episode.after: At fa4ebaa8b58be1e37ea623269ebf2c5d87437e7f, the desktop stage calls the Node prerequisite resolver before invoking the builder. The builder also retries prerequisite resolution when npm is absent and returns 1 with remediation guidance if npm remains unavailable. That nonzero result flows through the existing stage protocol as a failed JSON result, while successful builds continue to require a recognized desktop application artifact.
episode.diff: The single-file change to scripts/install.sh adds 17 lines and removes 2. It inserts check_node into the desktop stage, replaces the missing-npm warning and successful return with a self-provisioning attempt followed by an explicit error and return 1, and documents why an explicitly requested desktop package must not silently degrade. No test file was changed.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned implementation commit is fa4ebaa8b58be1e37ea623269ebf2c5d87437e7f, its first parent is 77bb64813cb987ad80236219a20c6cb549b40049, and it resolves PR/issue 36134.
The resolution modifies only scripts/install.sh, with 17 insertions and 2 deletions.
In the parent state, the desktop stage resolved installation layout and directory state, then called install_desktop without calling check_node in that stage process.
evidence_units.source: git show 77bb64813cb987ad80236219a20c6cb549b40049:scripts/install.sh, run_stage_body desktop branch corresponding to post-change lines 2481-2490

evidence_units.claim: In the parent state, install_desktop warned that Node.js or npm was not on PATH and returned 0, so absence of the required packaging toolchain was treated as success.
check_node accepts an existing node command, otherwise detects the managed executable under $HERMES_HOME/node/bin and prepends that directory to PATH, or delegates to install_node.
The post-change desktop stage calls check_node before install_desktop, restoring or provisioning the stage-local Node toolchain before packaging starts.
The post-change desktop builder calls check_node when npm is initially unavailable, checks npm again, emits an error and retry guidance, and returns 1 if the prerequisite remains unavailable.
The code documents that desktop packaging is invoked through the desktop stage or --include-desktop and that the application's own first-launch bootstrap must not request a rebuild of itself.
After dependency installation and npm run pack, install_desktop requires either release/mac-arm64/Hermes.app or release/mac/Hermes.app to exist and returns failure when neither artifact is found.
evidence_units.source: git show fa4ebaa8b58be1e37ea623269ebf2c5d87437e7f:scripts/install.sh, install_desktop artifact-selection block following the build command

evidence_units.claim: run_stage_protocol executes the selected stage in a subshell, captures its exit code, emits ok:false with the exit code when nonzero, and returns that code to its caller.
evidence_units.source: git show fa4ebaa8b58be1e37ea623269ebf2c5d87437e7f:scripts/install.sh lines 2505-2538 and immediately following return statement

evidence_units.claim: The commit records manual verification on macOS arm64: the desktop stage produced release/mac-arm64/Hermes.app and the installer could launch it.
The changed installer has valid Bash syntax and the patch contains no whitespace errors.
evidence_units.source: Successful local commands: bash -n <(git show fa4ebaa8b58be1e37ea623269ebf2c5d87437e7f:scripts/install.sh); git diff --check 77bb64813cb987ad80236219a20c6cb549b40049 fa4ebaa8b58be1e37ea623269ebf2c5d87437e7f

evidence_units.claim: No automated test file was changed, and the pinned tree exposes a PowerShell stage-protocol test but no corresponding shell installer test for this behavior.
evidence_units.source: git diff --name-status 77bb64813cb987ad80236219a20c6cb549b40049 fa4ebaa8b58be1e37ea623269ebf2c5d87437e7f; git ls-tree -r --name-only fa4ebaa8b58be1e37ea623269ebf2c5d87437e7f scripts/tests

candidate_atomics.name: restore-isolated-stage-toolchain
candidate_atomics.title: Restore the packaging toolchain inside an isolated stage
candidate_atomics.description: Re-establish a prerequisite in the process that consumes it instead of assuming PATH mutations from an earlier installer stage remain available.

semantic_action.intent: Ensure an explicitly requested packaging stage can discover or provision its required runtime even when earlier stages executed in separate processes.
semantic_action.pre_state: A packaging stage starts in a new process, and a tool provisioned by an earlier stage may exist in managed storage without being present on the current PATH.
semantic_action.post_state: Before packaging is invoked, the current stage has run the prerequisite resolver that discovers the system runtime, restores the managed runtime to PATH, or attempts installation.
semantic_action.validation: Run the packaging stage with the managed runtime present outside the initial PATH and verify that prerequisite resolution adds it to PATH and packaging proceeds to its build and artifact checks.

candidate_atomics.name: fail-requested-packaging-on-missing-toolchain
candidate_atomics.title: Fail requested packaging when its toolchain remains unavailable
candidate_atomics.description: Convert a false-success prerequisite skip into an actionable nonzero failure that the installer protocol can report accurately.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent an installer from reporting completion when an explicitly requested package cannot be built because its required executable is unavailable.
semantic_action.module_role: package build prerequisite guard and stage-result contract
semantic_action.pre_state: Packaging was explicitly requested, but its required executable is unavailable after the permitted discovery or provisioning attempt.
semantic_action.post_state: The builder emits actionable remediation, returns a nonzero status, and the enclosing stage protocol reports failure instead of successful completion.
semantic_action.validation: Run the stage with the required executable unavailable after prerequisite resolution; verify a nonzero exit and an ok:false stage result. On the success path, verify that the expected packaged artifact exists before accepting completion.

candidate_workflows.name: make-isolated-packaging-stage-truthful
candidate_workflows.title: Make an isolated packaging stage restore prerequisites and report truthful completion
candidate_workflows.description: Use this workflow when a multi-process installer can lose an earlier stage's environment changes and consequently skip an explicitly requested package while still reporting success.

workflow_graph.goal: An explicitly requested packaging stage either produces a recognized launchable artifact or terminates with an actionable failure that is visible through the installer protocol.
when_to_use: Installer stages run in separate processes or otherwise do not inherit PATH mutations from prerequisite stages.
A packaging stage depends on a runtime that may have been installed into an application-managed directory.
The current behavior can skip a requested build and still report successful completion.
anti_goals: Do not make optional command-line or first-launch flows rebuild the desktop application when they did not request packaging.
Do not treat signing, notarization, or distributable image production as part of this prerequisite-restoration fix.
Do not accept process success alone when the expected packaged artifact is absent.
Do not replace the managed toolchain policy with an unrelated packaging system.
not_applicable_when: All stages execute in one process with guaranteed environment inheritance and the prerequisite is already enforced at the packaging boundary.
Packaging is genuinely optional and the caller's contract explicitly permits a reported skipped result.
The failure is caused by the package build itself or an unrecognized output path rather than prerequisite discovery.
inputs: Prerequisite resolver capable of discovering, restoring, or provisioning the runtime
Managed runtime installation directory and required executable name
Stage result protocol that maps exit status to success or failure
workflow_graph.entry_state: The installer has reached an explicitly requested packaging stage, but the new stage process may not contain the runtime path established earlier and may currently turn a missing executable into successful completion.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The stage restores or provisions its runtime before building; if the executable remains missing it returns and reports failure, and if building succeeds it confirms a recognized artifact before completion.

steps.condition: The packaging stage runs in an isolated process and depends on a runtime whose managed installation may not be on the current PATH.
steps.validation: With only the managed runtime available, verify that the stage-local resolver exposes the required executable before the builder executes.

steps.condition: After prerequisite reconciliation, enforce the result contract for both unavailable-toolchain and completed-build outcomes.
steps.validation: Verify that unresolved prerequisite absence produces nonzero status and ok:false, while the success path is accepted only after a recognized package artifact exists.

validation_ladder: Run Bash syntax validation and patch whitespace validation.
Exercise prerequisite reconciliation with the managed runtime installed but omitted from the initial PATH.
Exercise the negative path with the required executable still unavailable and assert nonzero exit plus an ok:false stage result.
Exercise the positive packaging path and assert that one of the supported application artifact paths exists.
Perform an end-to-end installer launch check using the produced application artifact on each supported packaging architecture.
stop_conditions: Stop and report failure if prerequisite reconciliation cannot expose the required executable.
Stop and report failure if dependency installation or the package build command returns nonzero.
Stop and report failure if the build command completes but no recognized artifact is found.
Defer promotion beyond a candidate workflow until automated shell-stage coverage or equivalent repeatable validation is available.
unresolved_or_deferred: No automated test for the shell desktop-stage behavior was added or found at the pinned ref.
The commit reports macOS arm64 runtime verification, but equivalent Linux behavior and other macOS architectures were not evidenced.
Bootstrap-installer call-site blobs were unavailable in the partial checkout, so consumer behavior beyond the installer script and commit record could not be independently inspected.

unresolved_questions: Can a repeatable shell-stage test simulate a managed runtime absent from initial PATH and assert both the success and failure JSON frames?
Was the change exercised on Linux, macOS x64, and environments where runtime installation itself fails?
The GitHub bundle lacks PR body, reviews, comments, timeline, and status checks, so no CI result or reviewer-confirmed validation is available.
